problem_type: Native coding tool scope and approval authority
symptom: Installed skills cannot be read from the new lane, while project symlinks bypass the old lexical containment check.
direct_cause: Coding operations validate only lexical project paths and native tools have no capability registry identity for the lane approval gate.
class_root: The native assembly lacks a shared real-path boundary and a native effects-to-approval adapter.
affected_population: Native shell calls under every approval mode
internal_only_reason: Installed pi 0.85.1 source exposes operations, addedToolNames and before_tool; Nomi owns the project/package read boundaries and approval effects.
invariants: Read paths remain inside the project or a trusted installed package after normalization and realpath resolution.
Write/edit/mkdir paths remain inside the project after realpath resolution.
Unlocking tools never grants permission to execute them.
Shell hard-deny and mandatory-confirmation rules remain effective in every mode.
Pi timeout seconds convert once to Nomi milliseconds and back only at the local pi backend.
generality_proof: All coding file operations share the same pinned root boundary. Every native approval subject is derived from trusted effects and the existing shell classifier before the shared gate.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Pin trusted roots and check lexical plus canonical containment at every operation.
Derive native approval facts and mandatory shell constraints from the existing policy.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every read path passes the shared realpath checker; installed skill roots grant read access only.
Writes use only the project root, including nonexistent paths resolved through their existing ancestor.
Trusted native resolver may require confirmation or deny; tool visibility does not affect the gate.

recurrence.reason: Any installed skill, project symlink or deferred native call can reach the mechanism again.
same_class_scan: Inspected all seven pi operations factories and installed grep implementation.
Inspected laneApprovalGate subjectOf and codingCommandPolicy classification.
Inspected SkillRecord discovery and skillPackage symlink exclusion.

prevention.invariant: Only pinned canonical project/package roots authorize file operations; native shell restrictions cannot be reduced by menu changes.
prevention.failure_mode: Throw before filesystem execution or return a denied/awaiting-user approval outcome.
prevention.strategy: Use one operations-level boundary and one trusted native approval resolver.

legacy_paths.rationale: The existing pi operations adapter is replaced in place; no alternate file executor or skill loader is introduced.

dependency_lifecycle.target: A supported pi version preserving operations and durable addedToolNames contracts.
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: Keep upstream tool schemas and executors; application scope policy belongs at the provided operations boundary.
exit_criteria: Upgrade when pi changes the operations or deferred tool contract and rerun temporary-fixture containment and deferred replay tests.

migration: No stored format changes. Existing installed SkillRecord entries feed the lane index; existing lane active tools remain pi-owned.
residual_risks: OS sandbox still denies the settings root, including installed scripts within it; no bash read exception is added.
Canonical checks do not provide a kernel file-descriptor transaction against hostile concurrent filesystem swaps.

invariant_owner_layer.why: Coding operations are the first shared boundary with trusted project/package roots; the native approval resolver gives the shared gate trusted effects without changing upstream schemas.
